steps: The chemical energy in the muscles of the player is converted into the kinetic energy of the moving ball.
When the ball hits the window pane, its kinetic energy is transferred to the pane, causing it to break.
Some energy is also changed into sound and heat energy.
items.finalAnswer: Chemical energy changes into kinetic energy, which is transferred to the window pane and changes partly into sound and heat energy.

steps: Work is done when a force produces displacement in the direction of the force.
The man and the boat are at rest with respect to the shore, so they have no displacement with respect to the shore.
Therefore, the man is not doing work on the boat with respect to the shore.
items.finalAnswer: No. Since there is no displacement with respect to the shore, no work is done on the boat.

items.figure: Draw a curved valley between two hills. Show a cyclist at the top of the first hill moving downhill, at the bottom of the valley, and moving uphill towards the top of the next hill. Add arrows to show the direction of motion.
steps: Draw two hills with a valley between them.
Draw the cyclist at the top of the first hill, on the downhill slope, at the bottom of the valley, and on the uphill slope of the next hill.
Draw arrows along the path to show the cyclist moving downhill and then uphill.
items.finalAnswer: The diagram shows a cyclist travelling downhill into a valley and then uphill towards the top of the next hill.

items.figure: Draw two hills with a valley between them and a cyclist moving from the first hill to the next. Label the top of the first hill “maximum potential energy, minimum kinetic energy”; the bottom of the valley “minimum potential energy, maximum kinetic energy”; and the climb up the next hill “kinetic energy changing into potential energy.”
steps: At the top of the first hill, the cyclist has gravitational potential energy because of his height.
As he moves downhill, his potential energy decreases and changes into kinetic energy.
At the bottom of the valley, kinetic energy is greatest and potential energy is least.
As he moves uphill, kinetic energy changes back into potential energy.
Thus, energy changes between potential and kinetic energy during the journey.
items.finalAnswer: As the cyclist goes downhill, potential energy changes into kinetic energy; as he climbs the next hill, kinetic energy changes back into potential energy.

steps: Wood is a renewable source of heat energy if trees are replanted and allowed to grow.
It can be replenished, but it may become depleted if trees are cut down faster than they can grow.
items.finalAnswer: Wood is a renewable source of heat energy when trees are replanted and allowed to grow.

steps: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
Its SI unit is the joule (J).
The kinetic energy of a body is determined by the work done to bring the body from rest to its velocity.
For a body of mass m moving with velocity v: KE = ½mv².
items.finalAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion; its SI unit is the joule, and it is given by KE = ½mv².

steps: The law of conservation of energy states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be changed from one form to another.
The total energy of a system remains constant.
A body at a certain height has potential energy and, when released, begins to fall.
During the fall, its potential energy decreases while its kinetic energy increases.
Just before reaching the ground, its kinetic energy is greatest and its potential energy is least.
Neglecting air resistance, the sum of its potential and kinetic energies remains constant.
items.finalAnswer: As a falling body loses potential energy, it gains an equal amount of kinetic energy, so its total energy remains constant.

steps: Renewable sources of energy are replenished naturally and can be used again.
Examples of renewable sources are solar energy, wind energy and water (hydel) energy.
Non-renewable sources of energy are available in limited amounts and cannot be replenished in a short time after use.
Examples of non-renewable sources are coal, petroleum and natural gas.
items.finalAnswer: Renewable energy sources are naturally replenished, whereas non-renewable sources are limited and cannot be replaced quickly; examples are solar, wind and water energy, and coal, petroleum and natural gas, respectively.
